issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(...)` (see task text), but the template and the solution both define the function as `make_y_state(...)` (no leading underscore). This name mismatch is structural: tests and the template expect `make_y_state`, while the prose/instructions reference `_make_y_state`. Students may be confused about which symbol to implement or tests may refer to a different name than the one described.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent. Either update the problem statement to refer to `make_y_state(...)` (remove the underscore) or add a `_make_y_state = make_y_state` alias in the template (and reference the same name in tests). Ensure all task descriptions, template stubs, and tests use the identical function name.
